part.name: 4-bolt mounting bracket with clevis lugs and underside pocket
part.description: Monolithic bracket comprising an elongated base with four vertical mounting holes (stepped/spotfaced), a central pair of clevis lugs with transverse pin holes, sloped outer skins, and a recessed underside pocket with internal ribbing/filleted transitions.
part.symmetry_note: Approximate bilateral symmetry across the longitudinal mid-plane (in Z) for the base and mounting pattern; local features around the clevis/pocket show mostly symmetric intent but include asymmetric blends/face-splitting in the B-rep.

Section.name: Left mounting end (2-hole lobe)
features included: Mounting hole (upper/positive-Z) with stepped bore and spotface
Mounting hole (lower/negative-Z) with stepped bore and spotface
Outer end lobe curvature around the two mounting holes
Edge rounds/fillets at outer perimeter near the bottom face
Section.function intent: Provide a two-point fastening interface to the mating structure at the left end while spreading clamp load through a thickened lobe around the holes.
Section.physical behavior: Bolt preload is reacted through the spotface/shoulder and transmitted into the surrounding lobe; the thick outer cylindrical/lofted skin reduces local bearing stress and increases bending stiffness where the bracket transitions into the central web.
Section.geometry: Two vertically-oriented stepped bores (small through + larger counterbore/relief) located in a rounded/lofted end lobe; outer boundary formed by large cylindrical/lofted surfaces with small toroidal edge blends to the bottom perimeter.
Section.location: Left end of the part (low X in STEP bbox), encompassing the two left mounting holes.

Section.name: Right mounting end (2-hole lobe)
features included: Mounting hole (upper/positive-Z) with stepped bore and spotface
Mounting hole (lower/negative-Z) with stepped bore and spotface
Outer end lobe curvature around the two mounting holes
Edge rounds/fillets at outer perimeter near the bottom face
Section.function intent: Provide a two-point fastening interface at the right end; complete the 4-bolt mounting pattern for stable attachment and bending resistance.
Section.physical behavior: Bolt preload and external loads are transferred through the stepped bore/spotface and distributed into the end lobe; the rounded perimeter and blends reduce stress concentration at the edges under bending and torsion.
Section.geometry: Rounded/lofted right end lobe with two vertically-oriented stepped bores; includes toroidal perimeter rounds and large cylindrical outer skins forming the end profile.
Section.location: Right end of the part (high X in STEP bbox), encompassing the two right mounting holes.

Section.name: Central structural web / outer skins
features included: Intermediate planar facets forming the prismatic body transitions
Section.function intent: Carry loads between the clevis lug region and both mounting ends, while providing stiffness with minimal mass through sloped skins and blended transitions.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a bending/torsion beam: outer skins take tensile/compressive stresses under bending; angled facets spread stress into the end lobes; continuous bottom face provides a stable datum and improves torsional rigidity.
Section.geometry: Elongated prismatic body with multiple large planar facets (sloped/angled) and blended transitions; spans between the left and right mounting lobes and supports the clevis lug base region.
Section.location: Middle of the part, bridging between SEC01 and SEC02 and supporting SEC04 from above; includes the global bottom face.

Section.name: Clevis lugs (pair) with pin interface
features included: Two clevis lugs with transverse pin holes
Lug side faces and top/bottom trimming faces
Local ramp/facet tying lugs into the body
Section.function intent: Provide a pin-joint interface to a mating link/lever, enabling constrained rotational motion about the pin axis while transmitting shear/bending loads into the bracket body.
Section.physical behavior: Pin loads create bearing stresses on the lug hole bores (shear-dominated); lug plates act as short cantilevers tied into the central body, with the outer round profiles and fillets reducing peak stresses at the lug roots.
Section.geometry: Two parallel lugs separated by a gap, each with a cylindrical pin bore; lug ends are rounded via cylindrical outer profiles; multiple planar side faces define lug thickness and boundaries.
Section.location: Upper central region of the part (mid X), projecting upward from the central web.

Section.name: Underside pocket and internal ribs
features included: Internal rib/fillet network in the cavity
Section.function intent: Reduce mass and provide clearance while maintaining stiffness via ribbed/filleted pocket walls; avoid interference with adjacent components beneath the bracket.
Section.physical behavior: Pocket removes low-stress material to reduce weight; ribs/fillets help preserve stiffness and reduce stress concentration by smoothing load paths from the central web into the base.
Section.geometry: A large underside recess with a planar floor and multiple planar/curved wall surfaces; includes blended/ribbed surfaces visible in the bottom view.
Section.location: Underside of the central region (mid X), contained within the outer boundary of the base and between the mounting ends.
